title: Deep Learning-Enabled Supercritical Flame Simulation at Detailed Chemistry and Real-Fluid Accuracy Towards Trillion-Cell Scale
problem: Supercritical flame simulations with detailed chemistry and real-fluid transport have been limited to millions of cells due to computational cost.
motivation: Next-generation rocket engines and high-energy systems require high-fidelity simulations at unprecedented scale.
method: They created DeepFlame, a flame simulator that replaces expensive physics calculations with trained neural networks, dramatically reducing computational time. To leverage this speedup at trillion-cell scale, they optimized three critical areas: parallel computing (coordinating work across thousands of processors simultaneously), computational efficiency (streamlining calculations per processor), and data I/O (faster reading/writing of simulation results). The complete system was tuned specifically for Sunway and Fugaku supercomputers.
key_novelty: Deep learning can accelerate supercritical flame simulation to trillion-cell scale while preserving real-fluid physics accuracy on leadership supercomputers.
limitations: Specific to DeepFlame; limited discussion of general applicability to other physics simulations.
